March 1949

A-1

Treasury Financing Operations

March Certificates Refunded

Announcement was made by the Secretary of the Treasury on February 9 that holders of the Treasury 1-1/8 percent certificates of indebtedness maturing on March 1, 1949, would be offered a one-year 1-1/4 percent certificate of indebtedness. The maturing certificates totaled $3,553 million.

Subscription books for the issue of 1-1/4 percent certificates of indebtedness, Series C-1950, offered in exchange for the maturing certificates, were opened February 15 and were closed at the close of business on February 18. The new certificates were dated March 1, 1949, and bear interest from that date at the rate of 1-1/4 percent per annum, payable with the principal at maturity on March 1, 1950. Exchanges were made par for par and cash subscriptions were not received. The certificates were issued in bearer form only, in denominations of $1,000, $5,000, $10,000, $100,000, and $1,000,000.

Reports to the Treasury on the ownership of Government securities indicate that on December 31, 1948, about 61 percent of the maturing certificates were owned by reporting commercial banks and Federal Reserve Banks. The ownership figures for December 31 are the latest available for holdings of commercial banks.

Subscriptions to the new certificates amounted

Note: Details of Treasury market financing operations are shown in the tables on "Offerings" and "Disposition", respectively, of marketable issues of bonds, notes,

to $2,922 million on the basis of preliminary figures. Maturing certificates held by Federal Reserve Banks to the extent of $400 million were redeemed for cash, leaving $231 million held by other investors to be paid in cash.

Call of 2 Percent Treasury Bonds of 1949-51

On February 14, the Secretary announced that all outstanding 2 percent Treasury bonds of 1949-51, dated January 15, 1942, are called for redemption on June 15, 1949. The amount of this issue outstanding is $1,014 million. The announcement stated that holders of these bonds, in advance of the redemption date, may be offered the privilege of exchanging all or part of their called bonds for other interest-bearing obligations of the United States, in which event public notice will hereafter be given.

Treasury Bills Retired and Refunded

Treasury bills maturing in January totaled $3.8 billion, and the amount refunded totaled $3.7 billion. The issue dated January 6 amounted to $1.0 billion, which was $100 million less than the amount maturing. The other three maturities of $900 million each were refunded in full. The average rate of discount on the four January offerings was 1.155 percent for the issue of January 6, and for each of the others, 1.160 percent.
